_what: Resolution of the two identifiers that did not return under EXT_ID in the reference-metadata fetch. Both turned out to be WRONG IN THE PROSE rather than merely unretrieved.
_why: CLAUDE.md §4: a plausible story is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis. The plausible story was 'Europe PMC indexes preprints under PPR ids, so an EXT_ID query misses them'. That is true of one of the two and explains neither identifier being WRONG. The discriminating observation was a DOI-keyed query, and it cost one free CI dispatch.

⛔_finding_1_a_wrong_pmid_reached_a_manus.how_established: The DOI carried in the SAME prose entry (10.1038/s41591-024-03233-x) resolves in Europe PMC to PMID 39322717. A query for EXT_ID:39148855 returned no record.
⛔_finding_1_a_wrong_pmid_reached_a_manus.⚠: This is the 2026-08-07 failure mode recurring: an identifier that no committed source supports, attached to an otherwise correct citation. lint_citations was built for exactly this and could not catch it, because the number WAS anchored - it appears in the provenance ledger. ⛔ ANCHORING PROVES A FETCH HAPPENED, NEVER THAT THE IDENTIFIER IS RIGHT, which the gate's own header already says and which this is the first measured instance of.

⭐_finding_2_the_ATR_papers_foundational_.cited_as: PMID 37205599, described as a bioRxiv preprint
⭐_finding_2_the_ATR_papers_foundational_.the_preprint: Europe PMC source PPR, id PPR653036, doi 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578, and NO PMID. So EXT_ID:37205599 returning nothing is not a preprint-indexing quirk - the cited PMID does not identify this paper and returned no record for anything.
⭐_finding_2_the_ATR_papers_foundational_.⭐_why_it_matters_beyond_the_citation: The whole ATR route inherits its premise from this paper. It is no longer a preprint. Every hedge in this repository describing that evidence as unreviewed is now stale and understates the route. ⚠ What does NOT change: the ATR vulnerability in EMC is still INHERITED from the FET class and untested in this disease.
⭐_finding_2_the_ATR_papers_foundational_.⚠_author_order_differs_between_versions: Menon S is first on the preprint; Gracilla DE is first on the published paper. Use the author string matching the version being cited.
⭐_finding_2_the_ATR_papers_foundational_.⛔_CORRECTED: The part of this finding that STANDS: the paper is now published in Cancer Research (PMID 41811428, PMC13223543, doi 10.1158/0008-5472.can-25-2166, 2026), so citing it as a preprint is stale and understates the ATR route. The part that is WITHDRAWN: every claim that PMID 37205599 is invalid or identifies nothing. It is a real Europe PMC identifier for the preprint.

⛔⛔_THIS_FILE_WAS_WRONG_ABOUT_37205599_AN: RETRACTED WITHIN THE HOUR, by the drafting agent that was told to act on it. This file asserted that `EXT_ID:37205599` returns no record and therefore that 'the cited PMID does not identify this paper and may name nothing'. THAT IS FALSE, and a committed record already disproved it: `research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json` -> `europepmc_37205599` holds a verbatim Europe PMC response fetched 2026-08-07 (HTTP 200, 10235 bytes) to the query `EXT_ID:37205599 AND SRC:MED`, with `hitCount: 1`, returning pmid 37205599, pmcid PMC10187251, doi 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578, journal 'bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology'. ⛔ THE PMID IS VALID AND IDENTIFIES THE PREPRINT. Nothing was fabricated in the citing prose. ⚠ THE MECHANISM OF MY MISS IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED and pagination is RULED OUT - fetch-paper.mjs pages the whole result set at pageSize 1000. The one difference between the query that works and the query that missed is `AND SRC:MED`, which every working query in this repository carries and mine omitted. That is a hypothesis; a discriminating query is running. Until it returns, no conclusion here about an identifier's validity may be repeated downstream.
⚠_finding_1_is_now_UNDER_RE_VERIFICATION: If my OR-chained query could miss a valid record once, it could miss one twice, so the conclusion that PMID 39148855 is wrong CANNOT stand on the same evidence. What is independently checked and does hold: doi 10.1038/s41591-024-03233-x resolves to PMID 39322717 (Nature Medicine 2024, 30:3601-3613), and 39148855 is recorded in citation-provenance-ledger.json as `status: unverified_at_baseline`, i.e. prose-only and never fetched. ⛔ ALSO WITHDRAWN: this file claimed 39148855 'WAS anchored' in the provenance ledger and that lint_citations therefore could not catch it. A ledger row marked unverified_at_baseline is the ledger recording that NOBODY CHECKED the identifier - it is not an anchor. The claim inverted the meaning of the field.
